feature.title: Tubeless Insulin Pump War, Brain Monitoring Breakthroughs & AI-Driven Trial Screening: MedTech's Week of Real-World Results
feature.summary: The week of November 17–21, 2026 delivered a surge of concrete medtech milestones: MiniMed and Tandem both secured FDA clearances for 7-day tubeless automated insulin delivery systems, fundamentally reshaping the diabetes device market. Meanwhile, real-world deployments advanced across neurology, GI surgery, and oncology, with TECELRA's final SPEARHEAD-1 Phase 2 data presented at CTOS and the first U.S. RefluxStop GERD procedures completed at USC. AI's move from pilot to production continued, highlighted by Fujitsu and Paradigm's verified 89% reduction in manual clinical trial screening at Japan's National Cancer Center Hospital East. Collectively, the week underscored a decisive shift from regulatory authorization to measurable patient-level outcomes.

highlights.label: Biggest story
highlights.text: FDA cleared both MiniMed Fit and Tandem Mobi as tubeless automated insulin delivery systems with 7-day wear in a single week, triggering an unprecedented three-way race for the patch pump market.

highlights.label: Key trend
highlights.text: AI is delivering verified, quantified workflow gains in clinical settings—from 89% reductions in trial-screening labor to zero safety stops in a Lancet-published primary care study of 98 patients.

highlights.label: To watch
highlights.text: TECELRA's final SPEARHEAD-1 all-cohort data, presented live at CTOS 2026, will determine whether a 43.8% ORR in solid-tumor T-cell therapy can sustain commercial momentum and spur competitor programs.

articles.title: FDA Clears MiniMed Fit™ — World's First Tubeless Insulin Pump with 7-Day Wear and Zero Interruptions
articles.snippet: MiniMed received FDA 510(k) clearance on November 16, 2026 for its first tubeless insulin pump, the MiniMed Fit, offering up to 7 days of wear, a 300-unit insulin capacity, and SmartGuard automated correction dosing every 5 minutes. Cleared for patients aged 7 and older with Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes, the device delivers up to twice the wear time and 50% more insulin capacity than competing tubeless systems, with a phased U.S. commercial launch planned for spring 2027.
articles.result: 7-day tubeless wear; 300-unit capacity; FDA cleared Nov 16

articles.title: Tandem Mobi Wins FDA Clearance for Tubeless Automated Insulin Delivery — First 7-Day Infusion Set
articles.snippet: Tandem Diabetes Care secured FDA 510(k) clearance on November 12, 2026 for a tubeless cartridge and infusion set converting its Mobi pump into a fully tubeless automated insulin delivery system, the first cleared for up to 7 days of infusion-set wear. The system uses Control-IQ+ technology to predict glucose 30 minutes ahead and adjust insulin every five minutes, and notably requires no hardware replacement for existing in-warranty Mobi owners.
articles.result: 7-day tubeless infusion set; Control-IQ+ AID; FDA cleared Nov 12

articles.title: Fujitsu & Paradigm AI Cuts Clinical Trial Patient Screening Work by 89% at Japan's National Cancer Center
articles.snippet: A five-month retrospective study at Japan's National Cancer Center Hospital East showed that an LLM-powered AI system combined with Paradigm's clinical trial matching platform reduced records requiring manual review by approximately 89%, processing 22,334 patient records and surfacing 57 priority candidates from a lung-cancer cohort of 3,027. Physicians subsequently confirmed 51 of those as promising, validating the system's standardized, expertise-independent eligibility assessment across scattered medical records and genomic data.
articles.result: 89% reduction in manual review; 51/57 candidates confirmed by physicians

articles.title: Masimo smartSedLine™ Receives FDA 510(k) Clearance — Faster Brain Monitoring Under Anesthesia
articles.snippet: Masimo secured its seventh FDA clearance of 2026 for smartSedLine, a next-generation brain function monitoring system that delivers a faster Patient State Index (PSi) induction response and increased measurement stability under low-power EEG conditions. The updated algorithm processes bilateral EEG power and patterns to give clinicians earlier, more consistent insight into sedation depth, particularly for high-risk patients and those with vulnerable brains during the full perioperative period.
articles.result: Faster PSi induction response; stable under low EEG power; Masimo's 7th FDA clearance of 2026

articles.title: TECELRA® (Afamitresgene Autoleucel) Final SPEARHEAD-1 Phase 2 Results Presented at CTOS 2026
articles.snippet: US WorldMeds presented the complete SPEARHEAD-1 dataset — covering all three cohorts and 137 patients — in a late-breaking oral session at the 2026 Connective Tissue Oncology Society annual meeting. The fully approved T-cell therapy for synovial sarcoma demonstrated an objective response rate of 43.8%, with 31.9% of responders maintaining responses for 24 months or longer, and a post-hoc analysis confirmed MAGE-A4 expression level as an independent predictor of response and progression-free survival.
articles.result: 43.8% ORR across 137 patients; 31.9% sustained response ≥24 months

articles.title: RefluxStop® GERD Implant Debuts in U.S. with First Commercial Procedures at USC
articles.snippet: The first commercial RefluxStop procedures in the United States were successfully completed on November 4, 2026 at the University of Southern California by Dr. John Lipham, marking the FDA-approved GERD implant's entry into the world's largest medical device market. European comparative studies presented at the mid-November Foregut Society meeting showed outcomes significantly superior to fundoplication, and 5-year published peer-reviewed data support clinically meaningful results in a majority of patients, including those with swallowing difficulties who lack other effective options.
articles.result: First U.S. procedures completed Nov 4; European data shows superiority over fundoplication

articles.title: Sine Health Wins FDA Clearance for First Smartphone-Only Essential Tremor Monitoring Device
articles.snippet: Sine Health (formerly Nordic Kinetics) received FDA 510(k) clearance on November 15, 2026 for Sine, the first FDA-cleared essential tremor monitoring system requiring only a patient's own smartphone — no additional hardware. The app passively captures tremor data through built-in phone sensors throughout daily activities, giving clinicians an objective, continuous view of symptom changes between visits and addressing the critical monitoring gap for the estimated 7 million Americans with essential tremor.
articles.result: First smartphone-only FDA-cleared tremor monitor; passive continuous tracking validated

articles.title: BURL Concepts FOQUS™ Ultrasound System Receives FDA Clearance for Automated PFO Stroke Screening
articles.snippet: BURL Concepts received FDA 510(k) clearance for its FOQUS automated transcranial ultrasound system, which scans the entire brain for emboli in 40 seconds without requiring specialized operator skills. The clearance follows CE Mark approval and confirmed real-world first human uses in the Netherlands and UK — where the system successfully identified PFOs in 30 patients — establishing clinical proof of performance ahead of a planned U.S. commercial launch in early 2027.
articles.result: PFOs identified in 30 patients (Netherlands/UK); 40-second whole-brain scan by single nurse

articles.title: Lancet-Published Primary Care AI Study: 98 Patients, Zero Safety Stops in Real-World Deployment
articles.snippet: A prospective real-world study at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, published in The Lancet on October 24, 2026, deployed a conversational AI system (AMIE) in primary care with 98 patients completing full interactions — none of which triggered a predefined safety stop, and only one hallucination was recorded. Clinician evaluators and patients both rated the AI conversations favorably, and patient attitudes toward AI improved after the interaction and remained elevated post-physician-visit.
articles.result: 0/98 conversations triggered safety stop; 1 hallucination; patient satisfaction improved

articles.title: Wearable AI Predicts ICU Transfer and Cardiac Arrest 8–24 Hours Before Standard Hospital Alerts
articles.source: Stanford Medicine / Nature Communications (via Stanford-Harvard State of Clinical AI Report)
articles.snippet: A hospital-based study cited in the 2026 Stanford-Harvard State of Clinical AI Report demonstrated that a model trained on continuous wearable vital signs predicted patient deterioration — including ICU transfer, cardiac arrest, or death — up to 8 to 24 hours before standard hospital alert systems, with enough lead time to intervene. The finding reinforces the clinical case for real-time wearable integration into inpatient monitoring workflows, moving beyond retrospective analysis to actionable early warning.
articles.result: Patient deterioration predicted 8–24 hours before standard hospital alerts

articles.title: FDA Classifies AI-Powered Digital Cervical Cytology Imaging System and MCI Prognostic Software as Class II Devices
articles.source: Alston & Bird Health Care Week in Review
articles.snippet: On November 4, 2026, the FDA issued final classification orders establishing Class II status for both a digital cervical cytology slide imaging system with an AI algorithm and a prognostic assessment software for mild cognitive impairment, confirming special controls sufficient to ensure safety and effectiveness. The dual classification signals the FDA's growing regulatory maturity around AI-powered diagnostic software, clearing a path for manufacturers to access the 510(k) substantial equivalence pathway for similar devices.
articles.result: Two AI diagnostic systems classified Class II; regulatory pathway to 510(k) established

articles.title: Robot-Assisted Rehabilitation After Knee Surgery Shows Higher Functional Scores vs. Conventional Care
articles.snippet: A narrative review published November 20, 2026, encompassing 36 RCTs and 2,084 adults found that robot-assisted rehabilitation following total knee arthroplasty was associated with improvements in Hospital for Special Surgery scores, Berg Balance Scale scores, shorter sit-to-stand times, and longer 6-minute walk test distances compared with conventional rehabilitation. Wearable and sensor-based interventions also showed within-group reductions in cervical repositioning error and fear-avoidance beliefs across musculoskeletal pain populations.
articles.result: 36 RCTs, 2,084 adults: robot rehab outperforms conventional on 4 functional outcome measures
